Render-node headless compositor backend

Status: accepted, 2026-10-20.

compd has three backends: kms-live owns physical scanout, nested draws inside a host compositor, and headless draws a virtual output using only a render node. Headless is the offscreen test and future recording target; hardware behaviour continues to be tested on KMS.

The headless backend lives beside nested at compd layer 4. GBM/EGL opens the selected render node and verifies the EGL device identity. There is no DRM device, master, connector, libseat, udev or libinput. The virtual output is headless-0; mode and scale are explicit. Two offscreen GLES textures alternate, with full repaints after scene damage. A one-shot software timer caps frames at 60 Hz and stops while idle. Software presentation uses CLOCK_MONOTONIC and claims no hardware completion or vblank. COMPD_HEADLESS_REFRESH_HZ may select a lower rate from 30 through 60 Hz; the virtual mode and frame timer use the same rate. The default is 60 Hz.

The binding profile is headless; the default Bus service is comp-headless, with comp-<name> available through --bus-service for instances. Headless never requests realtime priority or negative nice, starts no XWayland, and leaves the desktop session environment alone.

Headless owns agent input authority without a VT; session locks still clear agent input, while KMS and nested retain their session-pause rules. seat0 is advertised with no capabilities, and human input refuses seat_unavailable. The agent pointer starts at output centre; absolute headless-0 moves clamp to the mode's logical bounds. Each Bus service has its own observation topics, window registry and presentation statistics.

Screencopy and Bus captures run after completed offscreen rendering, including on idle outputs. The normal picture excludes cursor elements; a second pass is made only when a capture requests them. Cursor inclusion is chosen per capture, including mixed requests in one frame, and an unavailable picture fails its capture rather than substituting another cursor policy. Capturing unchanged content does not count as a new presentation.

Deployment and recording

An instance is a headless desk: its own nspawn machine, noded, session bus, PipeWire and portald, with only the GPU render node bound and no VT, tty or seatd. compd-headless@.service uses the session slot %i, just as compd@ does: a console desk uses a VT number; a headless desk can use rec. Both read /etc/mixos/session/%i.env. Inside the desk, the compositor's Bus service is comp; each desk has its own node. The standalone CLI default remains comp-headless.

The component owns mixos-headless.slice with CPUQuota=200%; the desk's compositor runs there at nice 10. Desk provisioning places its portal, PipeWire, WirePlumber and encoder in that slice too. The container has its own quota, so the slice does not need a per-instance name. COMPD_HEADLESS_REFRESH_HZ passes through the session environment file.

portald's serve --screencast-max-framerate N sets the cast ceiling in 1..=120 Hz. It defaults to 30, preserving console sessions; a headless desk can request 60 through its portal unit drop-in. This ceiling does not change the compositor's refresh rate. These templates do not provision or start a desk.

Phase 4b acceptance measures presentation cadence: presented_hz is the presented-frame count divided by the paced probe's elapsed time, and cadence_missed counts presentation gaps greater than 1.5 requested intervals. Captured-frame uniqueness is measured from the probe's pixel frame IDs. The client-deadline missed count remains a regression guard only: two free-running 60 Hz clocks beat against that deadline without establishing a compositor cadence defect.

The Phase 2 plain Wayland EGL client probe (weston-simple-egl, with WAYLAND_DEBUG=client) created its first wl_buffer through wl_shm_pool. Its rendered pixels survived composition and screencopy, but this was a wl_shm fallback. Client DMA-BUF negotiation remains unproven; this probe does not establish the GPU-client DMA-BUF path.

Phase 5b publishes the validated headless render node in the kernel registry as the composite device for backends without a scanout binding. The DMA-BUF advertiser uses the native GPU binding first, as before, otherwise this node, otherwise the v3 flat format list (nested). Headless therefore advertises zwp_linux_dmabuf_v1 v5-capable feedback with main_device equal to the render node's dev_t, using the existing narrowed import format set. Mesa can select its hardware EGL driver from that feedback without a legacy wl_drm global. The GPU acceptance tests read the default feedback on a real Wayland client, compare its main device against the selected node's st_rdev, and require a tranche carrying valid format-table indices. The plain EGL client must create linux-dmabuf buffers and pass the existing rendered-pixel readback checks; this establishes GPU EGL client allocation, import and composition. The ced probe continues to record its actual wgpu adapter and attached buffer type. This does not establish hardware Vulkan WSI on the build workers: their only Vulkan ICD is llvmpipe and they lack vulkan-intel. On a headless desk with vulkan-intel installed, ced chose Vulkan on the Intel GPU and presented through linux-dmabuf even against the earlier v3 global (2026-10-21, recorded in the private journal); the Vulkan path depends on the ICD being in the desk image, which the image builder now includes.

The Phase 5b Intel render-node run observed a version 6 global from the current Smithay feedback helper. Mesa bound version 4. Default feedback named 0xe280, equal to the selected node's (/dev/dri/renderD128) st_rdev, with one tranche of 224 format indices. weston-simple-egl created linux-dmabuf buffers; screencopy retained its dark background and bright bar. Ced chose Gl, IntegratedGpu, Mesa Intel(R) Iris(R) Xe Graphics (RPL-P), Mesa 26.2.4, and attached linux-dmabuf buffers. Idle SSIM was 1.0 and typed SSIM 0.980828380141, with exact Bus text readback. No console reference was supplied for this run.

Phase 5 uses ced's real egui/wgpu window with a private noded and editd, so ced.state {text:true} can confirm agent-seat typing independently of pixels. The reference helper services/compd/crates/testkit/scripts/app_reference.mix creates a fresh document and places an 800×560 window at (80,60), scale 1, in either session; the console-desk reference is captured separately with that same helper. Before the first GPU run, the acceptance threshold is fixed at grayscale SSIM ≥ 0.99 for repeated idle captures and the console/headless comparison, allowing minor rasterisation differences while rejecting material layout changes. The known typed line must produce SSIM < 0.999 against the blank document, alongside exact Bus text readback. SSIM uses uniform sliding 8×8 valid windows, population covariance, Rec.601 luma, K1=0.01, K2=0.03 and L=255. A test-only ced launcher installs a log subscriber around the unchanged entry point to record the chosen wgpu adapter; Wayland client tracing records the actual buffer creation request. A shm result is reported as a weaker client-buffer claim, even when wgpu renders on a GPU. Software wgpu adapters are recorded explicitly and establish no GPU-client claim.

What the headless-only run proves, and does not (review, 2026-10-21): with no console reference supplied, the test shows a large, stable rendered change after typing plus exact model text; it does not check glyph correctness (tofu or a wrong font fallback would still pass). Glyphs are only pinned by the console comparison. SSIM at 0.99 tolerates uniform brightness drift: a +10 luma shift scores about 0.9955 at mid grey and 0.9988 at bright grey, so a brightness regression is within the threshold by design and must be caught elsewhere. The tested artefact is the test-only launcher, which compiles the shipped entry point from the same source; drift is a compile error, never silent. The first Phase 5 run chose a software Vulkan adapter (llvmpipe) with wl_shm; Phase 5b's device feedback enables the hardware GL path recorded above. Hardware Vulkan WSI is unproven on the workers and observed on a desk with the Intel ICD. Open follow-ups are the test's fixed post-typing sleep (retry once on an unchanged capture), the helper's leftover .session directory on failure, and its reliance on spawn merging the parent environment.

Wayland conformance (Phase 6)

canonical/wlcs exercises protocol behaviour: buffers, pointer and touch delivery, constraints, clipboard and selection, subsurfaces, shell roles and popups, output descriptions and supported extensions. It does not establish KMS, physical input or hardware presentation correctness. The baseline pins v1.8.1, commit 2b385328366de5db19521b9b3eef81861430d984.

The private wlcs crate produces libcompd_wlcs.so. It implements the C ABI independently, with the callback structure informed by Smithay 0.7's wlcs_anvil. No source was translated. The /256 conversion implements Wayland's signed 24.8 fixed-point ABI; touch_destroy auto-up is local lifetime handling (wlcs_anvil's touch destroy is empty). The file header and NOTICE credit the reference; its MIT licence remains in vendor/smithay/LICENSE.txt. It owns a fresh compd --headless child for each server, isolating process-global configuration, logging and GPU resources across tests. An inherited socket carries test requests and client descriptors directly to compd's event loop. That control socket has no listening endpoint; the child also listens on --socket wayland-wlcs inside its private runtime directory. Pointer events call the agent seat's existing policy-host injection path; touch uses that host's agent hit test on down and Smithay's held focus for motion and up. Refused delivery returns an explicit error on the control socket and is printed with the compositor log path. Window placement uses the native policy-host placement executor with a test-only entry point: unlike the operator verb, it permits deliberately off-output positions. All new entry points are behind wlcs. Callbacks wait for completion on the compositor loop. The extension descriptor is read from a live Wayland registry, including the advertised versions. Creation probes a short-lived child and reaps it to cache the descriptor before wlcs asks for it. The descriptor callback only reads the cache, including after stop; only explicit start retains a test compositor. Stop kills and reaps the owned child, and parent death also kills it after a wlcs abort. The adapter is compiled only with compd's wlcs feature and installed only on the headless backend.

Placement uses the requested wl_surface origin at screen (x, y). The shim converts through the native camera transform (world (0, 0) is screen centre), adds the committed xdg geometry offset to obtain the Space element location, then reads the public window row and checks that its surface origin projects back to (x, y). Successful checks appear in the gate output. Absolute pointer and touch coordinates use the same conversion, avoiding a half-screen shift.

There is a contract discrepancy in the pinned wlcs tests. display_server.h describes the window's left/top; both pointer_respects_window_geom_offset and touch_respects_window_geom_offset in tests/xdg_toplevel_stable.cpp:131,162 (and their v6 equivalents at 103,134) expect local input coordinates input - placement + geometry_offset, which positions the window geometry origin. They use offset (35, 12) and input delta (20, 30), expecting (55, 42). Under the explicitly selected surface-origin convention, the correct local point is (20, 30). Those assertions cannot establish a compd coordinate defect under this convention; they are a wlcs/shim contract mismatch. No test source or normal compositor behaviour is changed to conceal the discrepancy.

Build on a GPU worker, keeping wlcs outside the MixOS checkout:

git clone --depth 1 --branch v1.8.1 https://github.com/canonical/wlcs /build/wlcs
cmake -S /build/wlcs -B /build/wlcs/build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DBOOST_ROOT=/build/wlcs/deps/usr \
  -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS=-Wno-error=deprecated-declarations
cmake --build /build/wlcs/build --target wlcs -j4
cargo build -p wlcs --locked
cargo build -p compd --no-default-features --features wlcs --locked
/opt/mixos/bin/mix services/compd/tests/wlcs_gate.mix \
  --wlcs /build/wlcs/build/wlcs \
  --shim /build/mixos/target/debug/libcompd_wlcs.so \
  --compd /build/mixos/target/debug/compd \
  --output-dir /build/wlcs/run-1

Wayland development files, gtest/gmock and Boost headers are required. The first build used Boost 1.92.0 unpacked under deps, without a system install. The compiler flag permits wlcs's deprecated gmock Invoke calls with gmock 1.18.0. WLCS may replace --wlcs; COMPD_TEST_RENDER_NODE selects the render node.

The gate enumerates every test and runs four isolated processes at a time, each with a 20-second deadline, preserving JSON, process results and compositor logs in the output directory. It checks every name and outcome against services/compd/tests/wlcs_expectations.conf.mix; additions, removals and changed outcomes fail with a diff. The first observation uses --record --expectations <new-file>; recording refuses to overwrite a file. Disabled and unsupported tests are recorded as skipped. The flaky list must be empty: exemptions are refused, and every observed outcome must match. The control socket's 10-second read/write timeout is half the process deadline; transport errors name the compositor log before aborting. Conformance failures are recorded for later work; Phase 6 does not change compositor policy to fix them.

The first complete observation (2026-10-21) recorded 1,228 tests: 361 passed, 563 failed, 304 skipped, 0 classified flaky. Every failed case produced a complete JSON report; no case hit the gate's process deadline. Unsupported protocols use wlcs's wlcs-skip-test JSON property, even though gtest also records an exception for them. These are skips, alongside disabled cases.

The original three largest classes were xdg unconfigured-buffer errors (319), layer-surface invalid-state errors (79), and input-region assertions (58). The remaining original classes were 38 event timeouts, 24 missing-notification cases, 7 keyboard-focus cases and 38 other assertions or protocol errors. The interface name is part of every protocol error's identity:

  • xdg_surface, error 3 = unconfigured_buffer. Stable xdg-shell.xml starts this enum at 1: not_constructed, already_constructed, unconfigured_buffer, invalid_serial, invalid_size. Compd emits error 3 on correctly configured wlcs surfaces, for example ForeignToplevelManagerTest.detects_toplevel_closed, yet fails to emit it in XdgSurfaceStableTest.attaching_buffer_to_unconfigured_xdg_surface_is_an_error (the report says the expected error was not received). This is a compd defect: the configure/buffer check is misplaced, for a later phase. Start at vendor/smithay/src/wayland/shell/xdg/mod.rs:1673 (toplevel pre-commit check, posted at 1721), and 2067 (popup, posted at 2116). The hooks are installed by xdg/handlers/surface.rs:130,208.
  • zwlr_layer_surface_v1, error 0 = invalid_surface_state. The 79-case baseline class is on this interface, not zwlr_layer_shell_v1: Layer/LayerSurfaceLayerTest.surface_on_lower_layer_is_initially_placed_below/0 reports must ack the initial configure before attaching buffer. This is another compd configure-state defect, raised in vendor/smithay/src/wayland/shell/wlr_layer/mod.rs:576. Layer-shell XML defines zwlr_layer_shell_v1, error 0 = role separately: another role is already assigned. That check is at vendor/smithay/src/wayland/shell/wlr_layer/handlers.rs:84,85, with the sticky role stamp in wayland/compositor/tree.rs:170. Premature or sticky assignment there would be a compd defect, but the original logs contain zero failures with that interface/error pair. Calling the observed 79 failures role errors would misattribute the protocol object.
  • Input-region targeting and coordinates: the shim's surface placement and screen/world conversion are corrected above. Remaining input-region assertions exercise compd's native hit testing and are compd defects; start at services/compd/crates/world/src/surface/interface/core/hit.rs:478 (fitted surface coordinates) and vendor/smithay/src/desktop/wayland/window.rs (surface_under). The two stable geometry-offset assertions instead retain the documented wlcs/shim placement-contract mismatch.
  • Event timeouts, missing notifications and keyboard focus: these are compd conformance gaps in the native event, constraints, layout and focus paths. They have no protocol error code unless the individual report names one. In particular, pointer constraints miss expected locked/unlocked events; exclusive-zone layout can time out. The adapter's device refusals are explicit in the case logs and must be considered when tracing each case.
  • Other assertions or protocol errors: retained per case, including missing mandated errors for invalid buffers and unconfigured surfaces, popup placement/lifecycle and output metadata assertions. These are compd conformance defects, apart from the stated geometry-offset contract mismatch. They are not evidence of a protocol-permitted refusal of a valid client.

All failed cases remain in the expectation file; this phase fixes the shim and attributes runtime conformance work rather than changing normal compd policy.
